The mysterious orginazation known as Paradox has vexed law enforcement across the globe for almost a generation.

Claiming to have a net worth higher than the GDP of most developed nations; the coalition of elite grifters, catburglers, and gentlemen thieves that make up Paradox no longer steal for money; but rather to prove to each other (and the world) that there is nothing they can't do.
Putting their illict spoils onpublic display at so-called "pop up museums";  Paradox brazenly taunts institutions all while the public clamors for more.
They are everywhere.  They are nowhere.  And if you possess something they want… they are inevitable

When mystic energy awoke on Earth, the world changed… anything was possible. But just because anything WAS possible, didn't mean that anything SHOULD be possible. And so the government made rules. Laws. A means for US citizens to enjoy the benefits of the supernatural world in safety. But rules and laws are for lesser men. Men with limitations. Men who were not Seven.
There are many rumors about what Seven did to land himself in the infamous government oubliette called Lost Whisper.   But there is no doubt about what happened on the night of his execution.

Wards placed by the most powerful ritualists of five different nations... wards designed to not just prevent mystical interference with the execution, but to simultaneously obliterate Seven's soul so that it could never be contacted, resurrected, or otherwise used by someone looking to follow in his footsteps... failed.

Onlookers viewed in horror as the eyes of the US Army’s strongest mentalist popped like grapes. They screamed as Scotland Yard’s premiere occult investigator, the one who allegedly captured Seven, crumbled to ash. Seven’s body buckled and writhed against his restraints; his skin burning from eldritch electricity... and yet he would not die. He laughed.
